transcript.speaker: p-zoe
transcript.text: ok can everyone see the screen? i'm sharing the fixture model

transcript.speaker: p-diego
transcript.text: I can see it 🙏 a little small though

transcript.speaker: p-zoe
transcript.text: zooming in. uh, so this is rev B of the shaker base, the main change is the plate is thicker around the mounting pattern

transcript.speaker: p-kenji
transcript.text: how much thicker

transcript.speaker: p-zoe
transcript.text: couple mm, i'd have to check the sheet

transcript.speaker: p-diego
transcript.text: Did you run a modal check on it? I'm worried about a resonance close to the test band 😬

transcript.speaker: p-zoe
transcript.text: ran it yesterday, first mode is above the band, but not by a lot. um, maybe 15 percent margin? not great

transcript.speaker: p-dmitri
transcript.text: 15 percent isn't great. What happens if the payload is heavier than we planned?

transcript.speaker: p-zoe
transcript.text: then the margin shrinks. i'd want a rib, or stiffen the web

transcript.speaker: p-kenji
transcript.text: rib is easy on the machined version, harder if we go welded

transcript.speaker: p-carlos
transcript.text: From the floor side, welded would be a pain. Distortion on a plate that size is going to be a problem. Machined is better, even if it's slower!!

transcript.speaker: p-luis
transcript.text: also how do we get the fixture on the shaker, the bolt pattern i mean, can i actually reach the back bolts w/ a torque wrench

transcript.speaker: p-diego
transcript.text: Good catch 😬 In the model, you can't, not with a standard wrench. We'd need a crow's foot or move the bolts.

transcript.speaker: p-zoe
transcript.text: ok, yeah, adding that to the list

transcript.speaker: p-dmitri
transcript.text: I'd rather move the bolts. Crow's feet change the torque you actually apply.

transcript.speaker: p-kenji
transcript.text: agreed

transcript.speaker: p-diego
transcript.text: Moving on, cable management, what's the plan for the accelerometer leads? 🙏

transcript.speaker: p-zoe
transcript.text: clips along the rib, strain relief at the sensor end, i think that works

transcript.speaker: p-luis
transcript.text: the leads on the last one got pinched under the plate, *pinched

transcript.speaker: p-zoe
transcript.text: yeah, noted, i'll route them on top

transcript.speaker: p-dmitri
transcript.text: Fine. Anything on the schedule?

transcript.speaker: p-zoe
transcript.text: yeah, uh, battery enclosure thermal runaway containment moved. Battery enclosure thermal runaway containment was 10/7, it's now 11/4. so that one slips

transcript.speaker: p-dmitri
transcript.text: OK. Noted. Do we have a workaround for the test lab until then?

transcript.speaker: p-zoe
transcript.text: we can run the small packs in the existing bay. nothing bigger, uh, until it lands

transcript.speaker: p-carlos
transcript.text: I'll make sure nobody's testing bigger ones. Cell packs are in the cage.

transcript.speaker: p-diego
transcript.text: Thanks 🙏 and let's finish the fixture comments, we're running over 😬

transcript.speaker: p-dmitri
transcript.text: OK. Zoe, send the revised model by eow. We'll review again.

transcript.speaker: p-zoe
transcript.text: yep

summary.overview: Test fixture design review for the shaker base, rev B. Discussed plate stiffness and modal margin, machined versus welded construction, bolt access for torque, and accelerometer lead routing. Schedule slip on battery enclosure noted.
shorthand_bullet: rev B shaker base: thicker plate around mounting pattern
first mode above test band, margin thin (~15%), heavier payload shrinks it
add rib or stiffen web; machined preferred over welded (distortion)
back bolts unreachable with torque wrench: move bolts, not crow's foot
accelerometer leads: clips along rib, strain relief at sensor, route on top
Battery enclosure thermal runaway containment: was 10/7, now 11/4
small packs only in existing bay until it lands
action_items: Zoe send revised model by eow
Zoe add bolt access to the list
